post.description:
Claim an auto-registered device.

The device row is created by the HARDWARE on its first LOGIN. This
endpoint attaches panel-side metadata (name, location, section, …) to
that existing row and transitions the status to ONLINE (or OFFLINE if
the device is currently disconnected).

Keep an unclaimed device fresh while the panel has it open — the
frontend calls this on an interval so the pending device does not
go offline before being claimed. Returns the refreshed timestamps.

Rare path for pre-provisioning: create a device row BEFORE the
hardware has ever connected. When it eventually does, the LOGIN
handler will flip it to ONLINE.

DeviceCreate.title: DeviceCreate
DeviceCreate.description:
Panel-side claim payload.

The device MUST already have auto-registered itself (via Com 1 LOGIN)
before this endpoint is called — the server will look up the row by
`device_code` and adopt it. See `services.devices.claim_device`.

DevicePriceScheduleCreate.title: DevicePriceScheduleCreate
DevicePriceScheduleCreate.description:
All ranges for ONE weekday — e.g. 01:00–03:00 → 5000 and
04:00–08:00 → 7000. Outside these ranges the device's default
`price` applies.

DeviceScheduleCreate.title: DeviceScheduleCreate
DeviceScheduleCreate.description: Single weekly trigger: e.g. Monday 08:00 → power on.

DeviceScheduleRangeCreate.title: DeviceScheduleRangeCreate
DeviceScheduleRangeCreate.description:

DeviceSettingsUpdatePayload.title: DeviceSettingsUpdatePayload
DeviceSettingsUpdatePayload.description:
v2.1 spec (Com 6, "device settings"): toggle config + POS terminal IP.

All fields optional — send only what changes; `pos_ip` alone pushes
the POS terminal IP to the device through the same Com 6 frame.

DeviceStatus.title: DeviceStatus
DeviceStatus.description:
Device lifecycle statuses (v5 flow):

* PENDING    — hardware auto-registered itself against the server but
               no panel user has claimed it yet. It CANNOT accept any
               command beyond the auto-registration handshake.
* UNCLAIMED  — synonym alias kept for readability at API boundaries
               (not persisted; PENDING is the canonical value).
* ONLINE     — panel user has claimed the device via `POST /devices`
               and the device is currently connected.
* OFFLINE    — claimed device that has been disconnected / missed
               heartbeat.
* MAINTENANCE — claimed device deliberately taken out of service.
* DISABLED   — claimed device soft-deleted; only admin re-activate
               can bring it back to ONLINE state.
